text:
marta: FYI seeing a spike of 502/504s from api.edge in eu-west1 for users on IPv6-only networks. Clients hit the LB AAAA, LB forwards to us but connections time out.

sam: Any recent config changes on edge LB in eu-west1?

kevin: I pulled the LB config via infra-tool: it started advertising AAAA last night when we flipped dualstack for the new pool. edge-lb-bot shows a canary rollout at 02:14 UTC.

edge-lb-bot: Canary rollout: edge-lb/eu-west1/dualstack-advertise v2 -> v3 at 1700000000 by deploy-pipeline (traffic 10%).

marta: timeline matches. Symptoms look like NAT64 translation failing — downstream NAT gateway is reporting port exhaustion for tcp src ports used by translator. Mobile is IPv6-only so relies on NAT64 to reach our IPv4-only backends.

kevin: grabbing logs from nat-gw-eu-1: `sudo ss -tn sport = :1024 dst 10.0.0.0:443 | wc -l` shows ~11k ephemeral mappings, close to our per-instance limit. Also seeing `translation_fail` counters increase.

nirav: If NAT64 running on managed infra has limited ephemeral ports, dualstack advertise from LB increases concurrent translations because clients prefer AAAA. We accidentally doubled connection churn with the new rollout + a big model pull from gpu-pool autoscale.

sam: Is the GPU autoscaler triggering a lot of model fetches? That could create hundreds of short-lived connections to model registry which are amplified by NAT64.

kevin: Yep — autoscale event at 02:05 added 30 nodes, each warmup pulls model blobs in parallel (range 4-8 streams). Burst started ~02:06-02:10, matches the LB canary window.

marta: Short-term mitigation options: 1) roll back AAAA advertise in eu-west1 (stop advertising IPv6 to clients) 2) increase NAT64 port pool / add more nat instances 3) rate-limit model pulls during warmup 4) enable IPv6-capable backends for the model registry. Thoughts?

nirav: Rollback AAAA advertise is lowest-risk and fastest. Increasing NAT instances is okay but will take a few mins. Rate-limit model pulls could be done server-side but requires config change in scheduler.

sre-oncall: I can flip the LB advertise off for the canary group now. Will do a quick canary rollback to 0% and monitor.

deploy-bot: Rollout change requested: edge-lb/eu-west1/dualstack-advertise set traffic=0% by sre-oncall.

sre-oncall: Done. Canary rolled back. Monitoring ingress 5m window.

kevin: NAT64 translation_fail counters dropping, connection errors in logs decreasing. 502s down from 18% -> 2% in 5m.

marta: Good quick triage. Next steps: 1) schedule a proper fix — either make model registry IPv6 reachable from edge (preferred) or provision extra NAT64 capacity + port exhaustion alarms, 2) add autoscaler backoff to spread model pulls, 3) add e2e test for dualstack + warm-up traffic patterns.

sam: I'll add follow-ups in the eng-infra board and create a cost estimate for extra NAT instances vs. enabling IPv6 on registry (likely infra + sequencer work).

nirav: Also add metric: translations_per_second and ephemeral_port_utilization per nat-instance so we alert before saturation.

marta: thanks all :thumbsup: keeping this open until we have a plan assigned.

sre-oncall: assigning incident card to @sam and @nirav, priority P2 for follow-up.
